title: U.S. House · New York's 26th District
area: Western New York, including Buffalo and most of Erie County, plus Niagara Falls and part of Niagara County.

context.text: Both the Democratic and Republican/Conservative primaries for this seat were canceled; incumbent Timothy M. Kennedy and Dennis Hannon each advanced without appearing on a primary ballot.

summary.text: Timothy M. Kennedy is the Democratic incumbent for New York's 26th District, a Buffalo native and licensed occupational therapist who served on the Erie County legislature and in the New York State Senate before winning an April 2024 special election to the House. He sits on the Homeland Security and Veterans' Affairs committees and is seeking a first full term.

background.text: Born in Buffalo, New York, in 1976. According to his congressional biography, he grew up in a blue-collar Buffalo family with four siblings and attended St. Joseph's Collegiate Institute.
Earned bachelor's and master's degrees in occupational therapy from D'Youville College (now D'Youville University) in 1999.
Worked for 11 years as a licensed occupational therapist with geriatric and pediatric patients before entering public office.
Served on the Erie County legislature from 2004 to 2010.

In 2010, defeated incumbent Democratic State Senator William Stachowski in the primary and then Republican Jack Quinn in the general election for New York State Senate District 58; he served in the State Senate from 2011 to 2024.

In the State Senate, chaired the Transportation Committee, according to his congressional biography, which says he worked on funding for the Niagara Frontier Transportation Authority's Metro Rail, school bus and work-zone safety legislation, and limousine safety reforms.

Elected to the U.S. House on April 30, 2024, in a special election. Sits on the Homeland Security Committee (Emergency Management and Technology; Transportation and Maritime Security subcommittees) and the Veterans' Affairs Committee.
Co-chairs the Northern Border Caucus and introduced the SNOW Act on FEMA's response to winter weather events, according to his congressional biography.
Lives in the City of Buffalo with his wife, Katie, and their three children, according to his congressional biography.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Homeland Security (Emergency Management and Technology; Transportation and Maritime Security subcommittees) and the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (Economic Opportunity; Oversight and Investigations subcommittees) in the 119th Congress.

Introduced H.R. 9382, requiring U.S. Customs and Border Protection to link together family members' applications throughout the NEXUS trusted-traveler application process; the bill passed the House on September 16, 2026 and was sent to the Senate.

summary.text: Dennis Hannon is a technology professional and first-time candidate running as the Republican and Conservative nominee, a challenger to Rep. Kennedy. He launched his campaign in April 2026 and says his priorities are public safety, lowering costs and protecting children physically and online.

background.text: Says he grew up working in his father's construction business.

According to his Ballotpedia survey, he decided to run after becoming a parent and, in his words, fighting for his own child over medical decisions; he says he is running to put working families first.
Formally launched his campaign for NY-26 in April 2026 and advanced to the general election as the Republican and Conservative Party candidate without a primary.

priorities.text: Public safety, including strengthening cooperation between local and federal agencies, enforcing immigration and worksite laws, and cracking down on fentanyl trafficking.
Lowering costs, including tax relief for working-class families and lower prescription drug and healthcare costs, especially for seniors.
Child-protection policy, including online privacy protections for minors and opposing gender-affirming medical care for minors.

positions.summary: Supports enforcing immigration and worksite laws, focused on serious public safety threats, and cracking down on fentanyl trafficking.
